96987.title: Density offers Compact, Regular and Comfortable, Regular by default
96987.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • User {User-B} has the "Admin" role at {Location-A} and has never changed density. You are signed in as {User-B}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {User-B} is ZZAUTOTEST F1 Nora New and {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, with no lead technician.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST F1 Density Choices and {Work-order-1} is S1-702.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "List" shown, "Search" empty, no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
96987.custom_steps:
1. Look at the toolbar on the right of the Work Orders page.
  2. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  3. Click the density button.
96987.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: List shows no density button.
  • Step 2: Tech View shows, with a density button in its toolbar.
  • Step 3: the menu offers three choices, "Compact", "Regular" and "Comfortable", and "Regular" is marked as in use.

Developers also check this with unit tests: DensityMenu.spec.ts (lines 36 and 57) and WorkOrdersToolbar.spec.ts (lines 207 and 219).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View)

  • Key decision, Fields vs. density are separate controls: “List has neither new control and stays as it is in production.”
  • S6-R1: “Offer Compact, Regular, and Comfortable density in Tech View. Board View has no Density control in this release (S3-R11).”
  • S6-R5: “Use Regular as the default density.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

References from Design

Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), Work Orders.dc.html, export of 14 Oct 2026 (design library _ds_bundle.js), read 14 Oct 2026. The design names Tech View's control "Row height", with the choices Small, Medium and Large. Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 (design-difference sheet, answer 11) for the PRD's names, Compact, Regular and Comfortable, and this case follows the PRD.

  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), density menu title: “const densTitle = cards ? 'Card size' : 'Row height';”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), Tech View density choices: “const ROW_DENSITY = [['small', 'Small'], ['medium', 'Medium'], ['large', 'Large']];”

AUTOMATION: READY
why: Board View steps 4 and 5 and the Board View half of both results removed: PRD v71 S6-R1 offers density in Tech View only.
Steps split to one action each (5 to 3); every step has its own "Step N:" result.

Preconditions rewritten in the two-audience layout; the "Dev-layer test" line, Needs line, build name and Setup block removed (the how-to is SETUP-C96987 in recipes.md); the dev-layer note kept as one plain sentence after the results.

[User-B] and [WO-1] became {User-B} and {Work-order-1}; the separate [User-A] creator is not needed by the steps and was dropped. Example names kept (ZZAUTOTEST F1 Density Choices, ZZAUTOTEST F1 Nora New, S1-702).
Quotes re-taken from PRD v71: S6-R1 (changed in v71), S6-R5 (unchanged), and the Key decision sentence that backs "List has no density button".

The design note moved from the Source paragraph to "References from Design" with the 14 Oct 2026 export's own words; the Board View "Card size" note dropped (Board View is out of this case), and Chris Ward's 19 Oct ruling (answer 11) named.

96988.title: Density changes spacing and size only, never what is shown
96988.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technician {Technician-A} is active at {Location-A}, with Time Clock on and a Role other than "Office User" or "Time Clock User".
    For example: {Technician-A} is Esther Howard.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST F1 Density Content and {Work-order-1} is S1-702.
  • In Tech View's "Column Selection", "Lead Technician" is turned on (it is off until you turn it on).
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
96988.custom_steps:
1. Write down every column heading and every value in {Work-order-1}'s row.
  2. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  3. Compare the column headings and the values in {Work-order-1}'s row with what you wrote down at step 1.
  4. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  5. Compare the column headings and the values in {Work-order-1}'s row with what you wrote down at step 1.
96988.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the row shows a value in its columns, including {Technician-A} under "Lead Technician", a progress bar under "Progress" and an amount under "Total price".
  • Step 2: the rows are tighter (shorter) than at Regular. Nothing else about the row changes.
  • Step 3: the same columns, in the same order, with the same values as at step 1. "Lead Technician", "Progress" and "Total price" are still shown.
  • Step 4: the rows are roomier (taller) than at Regular.
  • Step 5: the same columns, in the same order, with the same values as at step 1.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View)

  • S6-R2: “Density adjusts spacing and the size of rows, cards, and their elements.”
  • S6-R6: “Changing density never changes which fields, columns, or values are displayed.”
  • Key decision, Fields vs. density are separate controls: “Density changes spacing and element sizing only; it never hides fields.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY
why: Board View steps 1 to 5 (card fields, card at each density) removed: PRD v71 S6-E1 says Board View cards keep their current spacing, and Board View has no density button (S3-R11).

In Tech View the same check uses an optional column: "Lead Technician", which S5-R4 lists as off by default, is turned on in the preconditions; Progress and Total price are default Tech View columns. No new behaviour is tested.

96989.title: Tech View density is kept after logout, in another browser and location
96989.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • You can switch to a second location, {Location-B}, and a second browser (or a second computer) is open on the sign-in page.
    For example: {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, with no lead technician.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST F1 Density Shared and {Work-order-1} is S1-702.
  • In Tech View the density is not "Comfortable".
    For example: it is "Regular".
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
96989.custom_steps:
1. Look at the toolbar and at the space around the card of {Work-order-1}.
  2. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  3. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  4. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  5. Log out.
  6. Sign in again as the same user.
  7. Open "Work Orders" and click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  8. Change location to {Location-B} (your initials at the top right > "Change Location").
  9. Open "Work Orders" and click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  10. In the second browser, sign in as the same user.
  11. In the second browser, open "Work Orders" and click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
96989.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: Board View's toolbar has no density button.
  • Step 2: Tech View shows, with a density button in its toolbar.
  • Step 3: "Comfortable" is in use and the rows are roomier than before.
  • Step 4: Board View still has no density button, and the card of {Work-order-1} has the same spacing as at step 1. Choosing Comfortable in Tech View did not change Board View.
  • Step 5: you are signed out.
  • Step 6: you are signed in.
  • Step 7: Tech View opens with "Comfortable" still in use: the rows have the same roomy spacing as at step 3.
  • Step 8: the top bar shows {Location-B}.
  • Step 9: at {Location-B}, Tech View is at "Comfortable" too.
  • Step 10: you are signed in in the second browser.
  • Step 11: in the second browser, Tech View is at "Comfortable" too.

Known problem (SV-11580, Open; planned for this release): until it ships, Board View still shows the density button and its cards follow the density chosen in Tech View. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, mark it Passed and tell the QA lead: the change has shipped.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, stories SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View) and SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); ticket SV-11580

  • S3-R11: “Board View shows no Density control in this release (SV-11580). Column Selection sits centered between the toolbar’s two dividers, with no empty gap where Density was. A Card size control as in the design (Compact and Detailed) follows as a fast follow (SV-11581).”
  • S6-R1: “Offer Compact, Regular, and Comfortable density in Tech View. Board View has no Density control in this release (S3-R11).”
  • S6-R3: “Density belongs to Tech View only. Board View’s fast-follow Card size (SV-11581) is saved separately.”
  • S6-E1: “Density applies to Tech View rows on Work Orders; Board View cards keep their current spacing in this release. List keeps today’s row size, and other application tables are unchanged.”
  • S6-R7: “Save density per user across sessions, logout/login, devices, and locations.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11580)
why: Title changed: the old title ("One density choice is shared by Tech View and Board View and kept") is wrong under PRD v71, where density belongs to Tech View only (S6-R3).

The shared-choice check (old step 2, Board View reads Comfortable) replaced, as v71 says, by: Board View has no density button (S3-R11) and its card keeps its spacing after Comfortable is chosen in Tech View (S6-E1, S6-R3) - steps 1 and 4.

The saved-per-user check kept in full (S6-R7): after logout and login, at the second location and in the second browser, Tech View is still Comfortable. Old steps 3 to 5 now open Tech View (they opened Board View in step 4 before).
One action per step (5 to 11); one "Step N:" result per step. Over the 10-step target; not split (Rule 127).

Preconditions in the two-audience layout; Needs line, build name and Setup block removed (SETUP-C96989). {Location-B} added as a named placeholder for the old "second location" (example Staging Lethbridge - 4310, from the setup file). Example names kept (ZZAUTOTEST F1 Density Shared, S1-702).
Quotes from PRD v71: S3-R11, S6-R1, S6-R3, S6-E1 (all changed in v71) and S6-R7 (unchanged).

96990.title: Tech View row text stays the same size at every density
96990.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technician {Technician-A} is active at {Location-A}, with Time Clock on and a Role other than "Office User" or "Time Clock User".
    For example: {Technician-A} is Esther Howard.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Compact Text" and {Work-order-1} is S10043-17651.
  • Tech View shows the "Progress" column (it is on by default).
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", nothing ticked in "Status", no choice in "Asset on Site", "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
96990.custom_steps:
1. Click the density button and choose "Regular".
  2. Look at the size of the text in {Work-order-1}'s row, of the column header labels and of the percentage beside the progress bar.
  3. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  4. Compare the same texts with what you saw at step 2.
  5. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  6. Compare the same texts with what you saw at step 2.
96990.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "Regular" is in use.
  • Step 2: the row text is the normal size (14 px). The column header labels and the percentage are smaller (12 px).
  • Step 3: "Compact" is in use and the rows are tighter.
  • Step 4: at Compact the row text is the same size as at Regular (14 px), not smaller. The column header labels and the percentage keep their own smaller size (12 px), the same as at Regular.
  • Step 5: "Comfortable" is in use and the rows are roomier.
  • Step 6: at Comfortable every text is the same size as at Regular.

The PRD (version 52) said only that Compact must not go below the minimum body text size, while the design's Compact rows use 13 px. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 27) that row and card text is 14 px at every density and text the design sets at 12 px stays 12 px; PRD versions 54 to 71 say so, and this case follows it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View)

  • S6-R4: “Row and card text is 14px at every density; Compact never shrinks it. Text the design sets at 12px at every density, such as column header labels (S2-R21), the progress percentage and secondary lines, stays 12px.”
  • Terminology, Density: “Design must define the three variants without reducing text below the application’s minimum body size.”

From: Chris Ward's answer 27, "WO Board and Tech View – questions for Chris Ward (14 Oct 2026)" (Google Sheet 1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU, tab "Questions for Chris"), answered 15 Oct 2026, read 15 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 27: “27. (a). Row and card text is 14px at every density, and Compact never shrinks it. Text the design sets at 12px at every density (column header labels, the percentage, secondary lines) stays 12px. S6-R4.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY
why: Title changed: "card text" dropped, because Board View cards have no density in PRD v71 (S6-E1).
Board View steps 9 to 11 and the Step 11 result removed (they set density in Board View, which v71 removes, S3-R11).

Old steps 1 and 2 (open Work Orders, search, click Tech View) became the starting screen; the Tech View text checks (old steps 3 to 8) kept, one action each (11 to 6), with a "Step N:" result for every step (it had results for 3 steps only).

Quotes: S6-R4 from PRD v71 (unchanged), the Terminology sentence the old Source cited, and Chris Ward's answer 27 as its own "From:" document, word for word.

  • Step 1: three thin outline icons side by side in a light-grey rounded track (a bulleted list, the head and shoulders of a person, a square board with three bars), the same drawings and size as in the design pictures, drawn in the same slate grey as in the pictures.
  • Step 2: a magnifier in Search; on the filters a circle of short strokes (Status), a clipboard with lines (Assigned to me) and a truck (Asset on Site), thin outlines as in the design picture.
  • Step 3: the Tech View button sits on a white raised segment, the other two look flat, and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey as in List.
  • Step 4: the density button shows three lines with an up-and-down arrow and the Column Selection button a rectangle split into three columns, thin slate outlines as in the Tech View picture.
  • Step 5: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 6: the density menu offers "Compact", "Regular" and "Comfortable", with "Regular" marked as in use.
  • Step 7: the Board View button is now the white raised segment and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey.
  • Step 8: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 9: apart from the Search and filter icons and the display switcher, List's toolbar icons look as they do in production today.

Until 15 Oct 2026 the PRD (version 52) left every List icon unchanged, so this case did not judge the filter icons. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 12) that the filter chips and Search use the design file's icons in every display option, List included, and (answer 21) that today's tabs, toolbar and Create Work Order button stay. PRD versions 54 to 71 say so, and this case follows them. The design names the three options Table, By Lead Tech and Board; PRD version 71 still keeps List, Tech View and Board View (answer 24). The Technician filter's wrench icon is checked in the Technician filter design case.

PRD versions 55 and 58 (S1-R9a, S2-R23; Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and PR notes, 15 Oct 2026) add that the display switcher's icons and the toolbar icons are the design's slate colour in every view, List included; steps 1, 3, 4 and 7 check it.

PRD version 71 removes Board View's density button (S3-R11), so this case no longer looks at a density button in Board View; the Board View picture is still used for the switcher and the Search and filter icons.

590128.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-06-tech-view-compact-light-1440.png" and "DC-06-tech-view-regular-light-1440.png" and "DC-06-tech-view-comfortable-light-1440.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by technician {Technician-A}, with a service advisor and line technician {Technician-B} on its approved line. On Board View cards the "Line technicians" field is turned on.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590128 Density, {Work-order-1} is S10043-17830, {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590128 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C590128 Ben.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
590128.custom_steps:
1. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  2. Look at the rows, the group headers, the avatars and the progress bars, and compare them with the Compact picture.
  3. Click the density button and choose "Regular".
  4. Look at them again and compare them with the Regular picture.
  5. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  6. Look at them again and compare them with the Comfortable picture.
  7. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  8. Look at the avatars on the card for {Work-order-1}.
590128.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "Compact" is the density in use.
  • Step 2: as in the Compact picture: the rows are at their lowest (36 px in the design), row avatars and the Service Advisor avatar 20 px, group header avatars 24 px, progress bars 48 × 4 px; the same columns and values show, the row text keeps its size and no hours line shows under the bar.
  • Step 3: "Regular" is the density in use.
  • Step 4: as in the Regular picture: rows 48 px, row and Service Advisor avatars 24 px, group header avatars 28 px, progress bars 64 × 6 px; the same columns and values show and no hours line shows.
  • Step 5: "Comfortable" is the density in use.
  • Step 6: as in the Comfortable picture: rows 64 px, row and Service Advisor avatars 32 px, group header avatars 36 px; the same columns and values show, no hours line shows, and the header labels and the percentage keep their small size.
  • Step 7: Board View shows the card for {Work-order-1}.
  • Step 8: the card's avatars are 24 px: the same size as the row avatars at Regular (step 4), and smaller than the 32 px row avatars at Comfortable (step 6).

The design's Compact row text is 13 px and the design adds the hours under the progress bar only at Comfortable. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 27) that row and card text is 14 px at every density and Compact never shrinks it, while text the design sets at 12 px stays 12 px, and (answer 18) that no hours line shows at any density. PRD version 71 still says so, and this case follows it.

PRD versions 60 and 61 (S2-R23; Chris Ward rulings on the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421, 16 Oct 2026) add the avatar sizes by density (rows 20, 24 and 32 px; group headers 24, 28 and 36 px; the Service Advisor avatar too), the Compact progress bar of 48 × 4 px, and Board card avatars that stay 24 px; steps 2, 4, 6 and 8 check them. PRD version 71 removes Board View's density button (S3-R11), so the card avatars are checked after Tech View's density has changed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View); ticket SV-11318

Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px.
